tool.title: Candidate translations — OPUS-MT (open model)
tool.description: Helsinki-NLP's OPUS-MT models (`opus-mt-<source>-<target>`), run locally, propose a translation for each string and append them to the catalogue's candidates sidecar with `source.kind: open-mt` and the model id. Seeds an empty `msgstr` with the first candidate, fuzzy.

install.cli: pip install transformers sentencepiece torch (or ctranslate2), plus one model per language pair, about 300 MB each

inputs.name: catalogue
inputs.description: The `.po` catalogue to propose translations for.

outputs.name: candidates
outputs.description: `<locale>/<catalogue>.candidates.json` (`translation-candidates/v1`), appended to; and the `.po`, where an empty `msgstr` now holds the first candidate marked `#, fuzzy`.

selection.when: Many short, literal strings; a run that must be repeatable (same model, same output); no agent session or no budget for one.
selection.limits: Sentence-level and context-blind: it does not see the term base or the surrounding paragraph, and some locale pairs have no model. Prose whose sense depends on context is better proposed by `translation-candidates-agent`.
selection.cost: A Python environment with PyTorch (or CTranslate2) and about 300 MB per language pair; CPU minutes per catalogue.

$comment.comment: `manual` for now: the engine script is being built in cat-harness-tools, and `check:tools` refuses a `bun run cat <key>` that no layer declares. When its checkout-script key lands, `invoke.shell` names it and `manual` goes.
The network is needed once, to fetch a model; a cached model runs offline. When the model host is refused, Argos models through `translation-candidates-libretranslate` are the offline alternative.
